newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Autistic boy's parents seek military flights ban.
newsitem.headline: Autistic boy's parents seek military flights ban.

text.p: The Belgian airforce may have to stop supersonic fighters flying over part of the country if the parents of an autistic boy win their court case against the ministry of defence.

The parents of Franky Sey in Ghent, northwest of Brussels, started proceedings against the ministry on Monday to stop jets from thundering over their house because the noise was seriously upsetting their son who is hard of hearing.
The noise "makes him hysterical, he could throw things through the window, smash up his radio," his mother told Belgian radio.

In a particularly serious incident the boy threw away his hearing aid during a tandem ride with his father after a jet flew low over them. The device was lost and Franky refused to wear another one, losing touch with his parents.

The family's lawyer told the radio the Seys were accusing the state of negligence. The argument that the state's defence interests were at stake did not apply since there were other cases where private interests had been allowed to prevail.
These included a summertime ban on military flights over the Ardennes natural park in Belgium's east so as not to inflict excessive noise on tourists.
The parents decided to take the ministry to court after a stream of complaints, even to King Albert, fell on deaf ears.
